Generate an outcome-informative visit schedule (C2)

Source: R/interval_censoring.R
visit_schedule_informative.Rd

Layers visit-process randomness that reacts to the simulated event time on top of a fixed visit schedule: a scheduled visit shortly before a subject's event may be missed at an elevated rate (miss_near_event, e.g. "too unwell to attend"), and/or an unscheduled extra visit may be added shortly after it (extra_visit_after_event, e.g. "brought in for follow-up after a reported symptom"). Both are optional and independent of each other; supplying neither is equivalent to thin_visits with p_miss = p_miss_base.

Usage

visit_schedule_informative(
  visits,
  events,
  end,
  miss_near_event = NULL,
  extra_visit_after_event = NULL,
  p_miss_base = 0,
  id_var = "ID",
  time_var = "sim_time",
  status_var = "sim_status",
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

visits

A per-subject schedule (data frame with ID/ time), or a common numeric vector (expanded per subject using events[[id_var]] – no separate ids argument needed here, unlike thin_visits, since events already supplies the ID list).

events

Data frame of simulated outcomes (typically the $events element of sim_tte_ode) with ID, sim_time, sim_status columns by default, after any add_censoring call (see "Pipeline position" below) – column names configurable via id_var/time_var/status_var.

end

Numeric scalar. An unscheduled extra visit (extra_visit_after_event) landing after end is dropped, not added – the same administrative horizon add_censoring uses.

miss_near_event

NULL (default, no effect), or list(window = <positive scalar>, p = <scalar in [0, 1]>). For an event subject (sim_status == 1), a scheduled visit v with t - window <= v < t (t the event time) is missed with probability 1 - (1 - p_miss_base) * (1 - p) – p_miss_base's background miss chance and p's near-event miss chance are independent, competing risks, so they add rather than one overriding the other (this collapses exactly to p when p_miss_base = 0, the common case). Has no effect on a censored subject, or on a visit outside the window – both use p_miss_base alone.

extra_visit_after_event

NULL (default, no effect), or a distribution spec in add_censoring's censoring shape (list(dist = "exponential", rate = ...), "weibull", "uniform", "lognormal", "gamma", or "user"). For an event subject only, one delay is drawn and an unscheduled visit is added at sim_time + delay, unless that would exceed end.

p_miss_base

Numeric scalar in [0, 1], default 0. Background miss probability applied to every non-baseline visit not otherwise covered by miss_near_event (i.e. every visit for a censored subject, and every out-of-window visit for an event subject) – the same mechanism as thin_visits's p_miss, folded in here so a caller does not need to chain both functions just to add a uniform background miss rate on top of the near-event effect.

id_var, time_var, status_var

Character scalars naming the subject-ID, event/censoring-time, and status columns of events. Default "ID"/"sim_time"/"sim_status".

seed

Optional integer. If supplied, set.seed(seed) is called before any draw.

Value

A data frame with ID/time columns – directly usable as add_interval_censoring's visits argument.

Informative assessment

This function's output is not a neutral assessment schedule. By construction, whether/when a subject is assessed now depends on whether/when they had the simulated event – exactly the situation most interval-censored analyses (Turnbull NPMLE, standard parametric interval-censored likelihoods) assume does not hold when they treat assessment times as ignorable. Using this function's schedule is appropriate for studying that bias (e.g. comparing a fit against thin_visits's non-informative schedule at the same nominal miss rate, as the vignette's "Interval censoring" section does), not as a drop-in, general-purpose visit generator. A message() naming this is emitted on every call.

Pipeline position

events should already reflect any independent right censoring: exact simulation -> add_censoring -> visit_schedule_informative() -> add_interval_censoring. Generating the schedule from pre-censoring event times would make the near-event/extra-visit mechanics react to a sim_time that the final events no longer has – the same ordering reasoning as add_interval_censoring's own "Ordering with right censoring" section.

See also

visit_schedule, which builds the base schedule passed as visits; thin_visits, the non-informative counterpart; add_interval_censoring, which takes the returned schedule as its visits; add_censoring, which should run before this.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- sim_tte_ode(model = "exponential", param = list(H0 = 0.05),
  n = 50, end = 24, delta = 2, seed = 1)
#> Loading model from cache.
sched <- visit_schedule(n = 50, every = 4, end = 24, seed = 1)
realized <- visit_schedule_informative(sched, sim$events, end = 24,
  miss_near_event = list(window = 3, p = 0.5), seed = 2)
#> visit_schedule_informative(): the returned schedule depends on the simulated event times; interval-censored analyses assuming non-informative assessment times will be biased by design (see ?visit_schedule_informative "Informative assessment").
out <- add_interval_censoring(sim$events, visits = realized)
head(out)
#>   ID  sim_time sim_status     sim_reason sim_time_left sim_time_right
#> 1  1 24.000000          0 administrative            24            Inf
#> 2  2 19.770560          1          event            16             20
#> 3  3 11.142509          1          event             8             12
#> 4  4  1.925641          1          event             0              4
#> 5  5 24.000000          0 administrative            24            Inf
#> 6  6  2.143028          1          event             0              4
# }
